title: Normalized quotient reductions of constant complexes
statement: For a commutative ring R, ideal I, and scheme W, use the constant quotient-complex model [def-a1-constant-complex-quotient-model]. There exist a finite tower d and reduction data e over W such that both are normalized. This includes the actual scalar coefficient cone, balanced associativity isomorphisms, scalar adjunction units, all transition squares, and naturality in scalar chain maps. No finite quotient or projectivity hypothesis is needed for the construction.

proof.text:
The constant quotient maps form a cone, so define the coefficient map by its
limit lift. Sheafify the balanced maps `a ⊗ m ↦ q(a) ⊗ m` to obtain the finite
transitions and their scalar restrictions. Tensor associativity identifies reduction
of the completed complex with the finite complex, sending `a ⊗ (b ⊗ p)` to
`a * pr(b) ⊗ p`; its inverse inserts the coefficient unit. The scalar adjunction unit
is `m ↦ 1 ⊗ m`. Define alpha as this unit followed by the restricted associativity
map. All transformations are natural before passage to complexes. The projection
identity `pr(n+1) ≫ q = pr(n)` proves the reduction square by the two tensor
universal properties, hence its unit square and alpha compatibility. Applying the
additive functors termwise preserves every differential and scalar chain map.
These constructions also cover the zero ring, zero complex and empty scheme. Use the scalar adjunction and the local tensor universal property.

lean.statement:
theorem normalized_reductions_exist (W : Scheme.{u}) {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    (I : Ideal R) :
    ∃ (d : FiniteTower W I) (e : ReductionData W I d),
      d.IsNormalized W I ∧ e.IsNormalized W I
